the-principles-of-aesthetics: Philosopher De Witt Parker asks a timeless question in this clear-minded book: what makes something beautiful? He examines painting, music, poetry, and architecture to explain how art works on the human mind and feelings. Written as a college text in 1920, it remains a friendly entry point into the philosophy of art for readers with no background in the subject.
study-and-stimulants-or-the-use-of-intox: A. Arthur Reade examines how alcohol and drugs affect the working mind — with arguments aimed at students and brain-workers. Drawing on science and example, he makes the temperance case in intellectual terms. A period piece now, but an interesting one in the history of attitudes toward drink.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aesthetics: A 1913 entry on aesthetics — the philosophy of beauty, in Catholic thought. Gerhard Gietmann treats the noble theme. Beauty is being's shining forth. Art serves truth when rightly used. A lofty subject, learnedly handled. The cathedrals prove its living truth. Its principles guide the Church's artists.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-apologetics: A 1913 entry on apologetics — the reasoned defense of the faith. Charles Aiken sets out its classic method. The Fathers answered the pagans' scorn. Reason serves the Church's cause. The science of the faith's defense. Its masters fill the patristic shelves.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-apotactics: A 1913 entry on the Apotactics — the renouncers of the early sects. Benedict Guldner notes their stern error. They cast off all possessions. The Church tempered their rigor. A sect of excessive zeal. Their rigor exceeded the Gospel's call. Their name means the renouncers.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-archontics: A 1913 entry on the Archontics — the Gnostic sect of the rulers. Benedict Guldner notes their strange error. They worshipped the cosmic powers. The Fathers refuted their fancies. A sect of the fourth century. Their books perished with the sect. Their aeons crowded the heavens.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aztecs: This 1913 reference piece on the Aztecs — the empire of the Mexican valley. Adolph Bandelier tells their rise and fall. Their temples smoked with sacrifice. Cortés toppled the bloody throne. The most famous Indian empire. Their calendar stone awes the museum.
